title: Diagnosis
description: Why a thing on a host does not work — the one contract the Linux agent (Go), the Windows agent (C#) and Bossman share. Deterministic: the agent collects EVIDENCE (single measurements with a stable id) and applies RULES that turn evidence into FINDINGS with a certainty. An AI may explain a diagnosis afterwards; it never creates evidence, findings or certainty. Prose description: docs/diagnosis.md; rule catalogue: configs/diagnosis_rules.json.

diagnosis_id.description: Unique per diagnosis run; evidence ids are only unique within it (an event record id repeats after a log is cleared).

status.description: The target's state when collected. For a service: running/stopped/failed/starting/not-found. For the updates target: up-to-date or behind (and failed when the last update operation failed). `unknown` is a named state (the agent could not read it), never a default.

summary.description: One sentence, built by the agent from the leading finding's claim — not by a model.

findings.description: Most decisive first. A target that is not running has at least one finding — `svc.unexplained` (certainty Unknown) when no rule matched.

timeline.description: Every evidence that has an `observed` time, ascending: what happened, and what changed before it.

gaps.description: What the agent could not observe at all, and why — so an absence of evidence is never read as evidence of absence.

name.description: The key name (Windows service name, systemd unit); for the updates target, the host's own name.

display_name.description: Windows: the localized display name the SCM events use.

evidenceId.description: Stable `source:locator`, e.g. scm:config:Spooler, evt:System:7000:184223, systemd:show:nginx.service, journal:<cursor>, lsa:rights:<sid>, authz:<sid>:<path>.

source.description: The interface it was read through: QueryServiceConfig, EventLog/System, systemctl show, journalctl, LsaEnumerateAccountRights, AuthzAccessCheck …

observed.description: When the measured thing happened (an event's time, a file's mtime). null for a state with no time of its own.

fact.description: One sentence a person can read, naming exactly what was measured.

raw.description: The measurement as read: event XML/EventData, registry value, systemctl properties, an ACL in SDDL.

certainty.description: Proven = directly measured (an exit code, a missing file). Likely = inferred from several measurements or from log text. Unknown = the cause cannot be determined; the finding then names the gap.

evidence_ids.description: Every id must be an evidence of this diagnosis — a claim without evidence is not a finding.

gap.description: Required (non-empty) when certainty is Unknown: what could not be measured.

precedent.description: The most recent change before the first failure. A correlation, not a cause: it never makes a finding Proven.

gap_seconds.description: Seconds from the change to the first failure.

remedy.description: A repair as data — never a script. Bossman exports it (Ansible, DSC, PowerShell) and files it as a proposal; nothing executes it automatically.

id.description: What it addresses: a service name, `<right>@<account>`, a path, a unit.

rule_absent.description: After the repair, a new diagnosis must not report this rule.

expect.description: The state a re-read must show (e.g. {"status": "running"}).
